description: We are a group of 9th graders from Rouse High School. We look to gain coding and hackathon experience from Space Apps this year, as it will be our first time. We're interested in creating something that will help benefit astronauts or maybe even everyday-people using NASA's APIs.
summary:
We built AstroVitals, a crew-health app for Mars-transit astronauts. An Apple Watch and iPhone feed a Body map that tracks five body systems and 16 common problems, from heart rhythm to sleep, infection and bone loss. Each person's heart rate is compared with their own normal, so changes are caught early. A rule-based Health check asks a few yes/no questions, escalates red flags, and updates the map. Colours run from grey (input needed) to critical. Every problem shows what to do, and an offline MedGemma AI answers questions without needing Earth.

It addresses the challenge by giving crews early warning and clear next steps when mission control is minutes away. It matters because on a long mission a small illness can become an emergency. AstroVitals is decision support, not a diagnosis: simulated data is labelled, and the crew stays in charge. Our project won 2nd place in our local competition.
details:
AstroVitals helps Mars-transit crews catch illness early and act without waiting minutes for Earth. It tracks five body systems and a 16-problem Body map. An alarm compares each person's heart rate with their own normal. A rule-based Health check asks yes/no questions, escalates red flags, and writes reported symptoms onto the map. Colours show urgency, from grey (input needed) to critical. Tapping a problem shows what to do plus a flight-surgeon reminder.

Benefits: earlier warning, clear priorities, guidance when help is far away. Intended impact: safer, more independent long missions.

Tools: React, Python (FastAPI), Swift (iPhone, Apple Watch), MediaPipe and three.js for an X-ray mirror (camera or Meta glasses), ElevenLabs voice alerts, and Google's MedGemma running offline via llama.cpp.

Creative: symptoms the watch cannot see are flagged "input needed", every screen shares one body view, and an X-ray mirror shows the problem on you.

We considered safety (red flags only escalate, AI answers checked, no drug doses), privacy (offline AI), and honesty (simulated data labelled; decision support, not diagnosis). It won 2nd place locally.
